text:
incident-bot: Pager: HIGH GPU_PRESSURE on dedicated pool catalyst-vpc-01 (CatalystHealth). Queue length 1.2k, avg latency 1.9s -> SLO breach risk. Escalation: oncall ryan-oncall.
ryan-oncall: Ack, I'm on it. Pulling metrics and checking pool state.
jess-infra: I'm seeing 98% GPU util on all 6 nodes, 400+ queued jobs per node. No node failures.
maya-ml: Model is candela-2.1 serving at 2k tokens/req for many flows — heavy long-context calls from Catalyst. Any possibility to fallback to candela-1.4 lower-cost model for non-critical routes?
ryan-oncall: Good idea. But Catalyst has strict VPC/dedicated isolation; we can't push cross-tenant fallback without their sign-off.
nana-cs: @ryan-oncall pinged Catalyst ops (catalyst-ops) — we need permission for mitigations that impact results.
catalyst-ops: Confirmed. We're seeing degraded UX in prod. We can tolerate slightly different model for background tasks (summaries) but not for direct clinical responses.
jess-infra: Two immediate options: 1) Burst: temporary add 2 preemptible GPUs to the dedicated pool (requires billing/approval), 2) Evict idle sessions and tighten concurrency limits per session. Which do we want first?
ryan-oncall: Start eviction and concurrency caps now. I'll request burst approval simultaneously.
jess-infra: Running eviction script (LRU, sessions idle > 60s). Command:
```
./infra/drain_pool.sh --pool catalyst-vpc-01 --strategy lru --idle-seconds 60 --dry-run=false
```
jess-infra: Eviction started — freeing ~120 slots so far. Queue dropped to 980.
ryan-oncall: Applying temporary concurrency cap per-session to 2 for catalyst-prod routes.
jess-infra: Cap applied via route config:
```json
{"route":"/v1/catalyst/*","session_concurrency":2}
```
ryan-oncall: Noted. Also opening burst request to finance approval so we can spin up 2 preemptible nodes. @dan-manager can you approve? This will be charged to Catalyst overage per contract emergency clause.
dan-manager: Approve burst for up to 2 preemptible GPUs for up to 4 hours. Notify legal/CS for billing.
nana-cs: Notifying Catalyst account team and confirming they accept burst charge. @catalyst-ops please confirm acceptance.
catalyst-ops: We accept burst charge for emergency capacity. Please proceed.
jess-infra: Triggering burst API:
```
curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwood/v1/pools/catalyst-vpc-01/burst \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $INTERNAL_TOKEN" \
 -d '{"count":2,"type":"preemptible","ttl_minutes":240,"reason":"prod queue emergency"}'
```
jess-infra: Burst request accepted by autoscaler. New nodes provisioning — ETA ~3m.
maya-ml: While nodes come up, enable model-level graceful degradation for non-clinical routes: reroute /summaries -> candela-1.4-quant. Need a quick route map change.
ryan-oncall: Done. Route updated. Queue down to 620, latency 1.1s.
jess-infra: New preemptibles are online. GPU util drops to 72% across pool. Queue now 180.
ryan-oncall: Good. Keep monitoring. Logging action for postmortem and cost reconciliation.
lena-prodops: Creating incident ticket and adding timeline, adding follow-up: (1) update autoscale thresholds to allow one emergency preemptible without manual approval, (2) work with Sales/CS on clearer overage flows.
dan-manager: Also schedule a runbook update: clarity on which model classes can be auto-fallback for Catalyst-like customers.
nana-cs: Catalyst ops confirmed degraded metrics resolved. They will run smoke tests and report in 30m.
catalyst-ops: Smoke tests passed. Thanks. Please include the exact eviction list and timing in the postmortem.
ryan-oncall: Will collect all logs + eviction list. Assigning action owners: @jess-infra (eviction script tuning), @maya-ml (fallback model policy), @lena-prodops (autoscale policy change), @ana-cs (billing + customer comms).
incident-bot: Incident update recorded: SEV2 -> mitigation successful, monitoring. Postmortem required.
ryan-oncall: Closing hands-off. Leaving monitoring on for 2 hours, will escalate if queues back above 500.
